rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s wives have the honor of marriage to him, but divine honor depends on piety, as illustrated by the reward and accountability stated for them.
rows.anchor: فإنهن وإن كن مشرفات بشرف زوجية النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لكن الكرامة عند الله بالتقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The replacement wives are described as Muslim, believing, devout, repentant, worshipping, fasting, previously married, and virgins; the qualities distinguish them from the current wives.
rows.anchor: مسلمات مؤمنات قانتات تائبات عابدات سائحات - أي صائمات - ثيبات وأبكارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The replacements would be better only through their distinguishing obedience and repentance, or obedience alone, while sharing the other listed qualities.
rows.anchor: كانت خيرا منهن وليس إلا لأجل اختصاص منها بالقنوت والتوبة أو القنوت فقط مع مشاركتها لهن في باقي الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qunūt means maintaining obedience with humility.
rows.anchor: والقنوت هو لزوم الطاعة مع الخضوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to Mary at the end of the sūra supports this sense: what the wives lacked was obedience to the Prophet as obedience to God, and avoiding disobedience and harm to him.
rows.anchor: فالقنوت هو الذي يفقدنه وهو لزومهن طاعة النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the view that later wives are better merely because marrying the Prophet confers honor; if that sufficed, the listed qualities would be irrelevant.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنه لو كان ملاك ما ذكر في الآية من الخير هو الزوجية كان كل من تزوج صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من النساء أفضل

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf explains that the attributes lack conjunctions because only previously married and virgin women are mutually exclusive; the other attributes can coexist.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف فإن قلت لم أخليت الصفات كلها عن العاطف ووسط بين الثيبات والأبكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qū is an imperative from wiqāya: to protect something from what harms or injures it.
rows.anchor: أمر من الوقاية بمعنى حفظ الشيء مما يؤذيه ويضره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa on the wāw, waqūd names the material used to kindle a fire, such as firewood.
rows.anchor: والوقود بفتح الواو اسم لما توقد به النار من حطب ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire is Hell; people being its fuel means that they themselves burn in it, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالنار نار جهنم وكون الناس المعذبين فيها وقودا لها معناه اشتعال الناس فيها بأنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted accounts vary in wording and routes, and their fit with these verses as one coherent passage is unclear.
rows.anchor: والحديث مروي بطرق متشتتة وألفاظ مختلفة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Ḥafṣa found the Prophet with his concubine in her home, became upset, and he promised to please her by declaring the concubine forbidden; Ḥafṣa told ʿĀʾisha, and revelation followed.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن سعد وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس قال كانت عائشة وحفصة متحابتين فذهبت حفصة إلى بيت أبيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the first report does not clearly fit the verse’s statement that the Prophet disclosed part of the matter and withheld part.
rows.anchor: أقول انطباق ما في الحديث على الآيات وخاصة قوله

words: وإذ أسر النبي إلى بعض أزواجه حديثا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet told Ḥafṣa, after she found him with Māriya, that her father would assume leadership after Abū Bakr; she told ʿĀʾisha, who demanded that he forbid Māriya, and revelation followed.
rows.anchor: وفيه أخرج الطبراني وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second report also leaves unexplained what the Prophet disclosed and what he withheld.
rows.anchor: وهي مع ذلك لا تزيل إبهام قوله تعالى

words: لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most accounts say the Prophet forbade Māriya because of Ḥafṣa, not ʿĀʾisha; they identify Ḥafṣa as the wife asking who informed him, concerned that her secret had been disclosed, yet still do not resolve the verse’s ambiguity.
rows.anchor: وفي أكثرها أنه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم حرم مارية على نفسه لقول حفصة لا لقول عائشة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says that a noble person never presses a matter, referring to God’s description of the Prophet as disclosing part and overlooking part.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال ما استقصى كريم قط لأن الله يقول

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن عباس
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn ʿAbbās identify the disclosed matter as Māriya and the withheld matter as the news that their fathers would rule after the Prophet, which he feared would spread.
rows.anchor: عن أبي حاتم عن مجاهد، وابن مردويه عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In a report transmitted by Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUmar identifies the two wives as ʿĀʾisha and Ḥafṣa, recounts how Medinan wives taught women to answer their husbands, then hears that the Prophet has separated from his wives and visits him.
rows.anchor: وقد روي بعدة طرق عن عمر بن الخطاب سبب نزول الآيات ولم يذكر ذلك ففي عدة من جوامع الحديث

words: لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك
rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar describes admonishing Ḥafṣa to stop rebuking and questioning the Prophet, then asks him about the household’s austerity and hears that Persian and Roman comforts are hastened to them in worldly life.
rows.anchor: فقلت لحفصة لا تراجعي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم ولا تسأليه شيئا

words: لم تحرم ما أحل الله لك
rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: The account says the Prophet had vowed not to enter his wives’ rooms for a month, after which God reproached him and prescribed expiation for the oath.
rows.anchor: وكان قد أقسم أن لا يدخل على أزواجه شهرا فعاتبه الله في ذلك وجعل له كفارة اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says ʿUmar’s account neither identifies the disclosed and withheld news nor fits the prohibition as applying to all the wives; it also fails to explain the specific appeal to the two wives.
rows.anchor: والرواية - كما ترى - لا تذكر ما أسره النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: In the Tafsīr al-Qummī report from Abū Baṣīr, Abū Jaʿfar identifies صالح المؤمنين as ʿAlī.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير القمي بإسناده عن أبي بصير قال سمعت أبا جعفر عليه السلام يقول

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asmāʾ bt. ʿUmays reports that the Prophet identified صالح المؤمنين as ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib.
rows.anchor: وفي الدر المنثور أخرج ابن مردويه عن أسماء بنت عميس سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Burhān cites the Abū Baṣīr report and says Muḥammad b. al-ʿAbbās collected fifty-two reports on the identification from both Shīʿī and Sunnī sources.
rows.anchor: ذكر صاحب البرهان بعد إيراد رواية أبي بصير السابقة أن محمد بن العباس أورد في هذا المعنى اثنين وخمسين حديثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He challenges the claim that a heavenly book promises them whatever they choose, whether in the afterlife or without qualification, and therefore grants them happiness and Paradise.
rows.anchor: بل ألكم كتاب سماوي تقرأون فيه إن لكم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aymān is the plural of yamīn, meaning an oath; bulūgh is reaching completion or fullness.
rows.anchor: الأيمان جمع يمين وهو القسم

words: أيمان علينا بالغة إلى يوم القيامة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describes emphatic oaths made by God to them, extending to the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فالأيمان البالغة هي المؤكدة نهاية التوكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis makes “until the Day of Resurrection” a stable adverbial attached to an implied phrase: oaths existing until that day.
rows.anchor: على هذا ظرف مستقر متعلق بمقدر والتقدير أم لكم علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the time phrase may modify “reaching,” with the oaths’ duration extending through time to the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: متعلقا ببالغة والمراد ببلوغ الأيمان انطباقها على امتداد الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret the oaths as covenants or pledges, using an associated term for the thing meant or a part for the whole.
rows.anchor: وقد فسروا الأيمان بالعهود والمواثيق فيكون من باب إطلاق اللازم وإرادة الملزوم كناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed figure treats “oaths” as a part standing for the whole covenant.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون من باب إطلاق الجزء وإرادة الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is the oath’s answer and states what was allegedly promised; the question is rhetorical denial of such a guarantee.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم وهو المعاهد عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address turns from the disbelievers to the Prophet because they have fallen below the dignity of direct address; the remaining questions are phrased in the third person.
rows.anchor: إعراض عن خطابهم والتفات إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم بتوجيه الخطاب لسقوطهم عن درجة استحقاق الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A zaʿīm is the person undertaking or managing an affair; the question asks which of them supports the equality they claim, a plainly absurd position.
rows.anchor: والزعيم القائم بالأمر المتصدي له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This challenges the possibility that their equality claim rests on supposed gods sharing God’s lordship and interceding to make them like Muslims.
rows.anchor: رد لهم على تقدير أن يكون حكمهم بالتساوي مبنيا على دعواهم أن لهم آلهة يشاركون الله سبحانه في الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to bring their partners is a figure of speech denying that such partners exist and reinforces the preceding negation.
rows.anchor: كناية عن انتفاء الشركاء يفيد تأكيد ما في قوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the partners to mean people sharing the claim and holding the same doctrine; the author says this would not settle the dispute.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالشركاء شركاؤهم في هذا القول

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second view takes the partners as witnesses for the claim; the author rejects it as unsupported by the wording and redundant after the book and oath possibilities were denied.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالشركاء الشهداء والمعنى أم لهم شهداء على هذا القول فليأتوا بهم إن كانوا صادقين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third view takes the partners as their alleged gods, brought at the Resurrection to testify or intercede; the author says this too does not end the dispute.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالشركاء شركاء الألوهية على ما يزعمون لكن المعني من إتيانهم بهم إتيانهم بهم يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yawm is an adverb of time attached to an omitted imperative such as “remember.”
rows.anchor: يوم ظرف متعلق بمحذوف كاذكر ونحوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uncovering the shin is a metaphor for an extreme crisis, since people roll up their sleeves when hard pressed to work or flee.
rows.anchor: والكشف عن الساق تمثيل في اشتداد الأمر اشتدادا بالغا لما أنهم كانوا يشمرون عن سوقهم إذا اشتد الأمر

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf reads the phrase as the intensification of crisis, with no literal uncovering or shin, like describing a miser’s hand as shackled though no hand or shackle is meant.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشاف فمعنى { يوم يكشف عن ساق } في معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These five verses interrupt the discussion because the alleged partners were supposed to secure happiness after resurrection; there are no partners or intercession, and afterlife felicity comes from worldly submission to God’s unity in lordship.
rows.anchor: والآية وما بعدها إلى تمام خمس آيات اعتراض وقع في البين بمناسبة ذكر شركائهم الذين يزعمون أنهم سيسعدونهم لو كان هناك بعث وحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers cannot prostrate in the afterlife because arrogance became an established trait in their hidden selves; on that day inner realities are exposed.
rows.anchor: فلا يستطيعون لاستقرار ملكة الاستكبار في سرائرهم واليوم تبلى السرائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Their eyes humbled” and “humiliation overwhelms them” are two circumstantial clauses describing those summoned; humility is assigned to the eyes because its effects appear there.
rows.anchor: حالان من نائب فاعل يدعون أي حال كون أبصارهم خاشعة وحال كونهم يغشاهم الذلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humiliation overwhelms them coercively.
rows.anchor: وحال كونهم يغشاهم الذلة بقهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of “safe” is that they were free in worldly life from the afflictions that later deprived their souls of the capacity to answer truth.
rows.anchor: المراد بالسلامة سلامتهم من الآفات والعاهات التي لحقت نفوسهم بسبب الاستكبار عن الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “safe” means simply that they had the ability to prostrate in worldly life.
rows.anchor: أو المراد مطلق استطاعتهم منه في الدنيا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The proposed interpretation that prostration means ritual prayer is dismissed by the author.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالسجود الصلاة وهو كما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Leave Me with the one who denies this Reminder” means God alone will deal with them; it comforts the Prophet and threatens the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: كناية عن أنه يكفيهم وحده وهو غير تاركهم وفيه نوع تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وتهديد للمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Reminder in this passage is the Noble Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: المراد بهذا الحديث القرآن الكريم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istidrāj is drawing them down degree by degree until their misery is complete and they fall into destruction.
rows.anchor: والاستدراج هو استنزالهم درجة فدرجة حتى يتم لهم الشقاء فيقعوا في ورطة الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gradual taking works by granting successive blessings; each keeps them occupied, makes them neglect gratitude and forget God, and distances them further from His remembrance.
rows.anchor: وذلك بأن يؤتيهم الله نعمة بعد نعمة وكلما أوتوا نعمة اشتغلوا بها وفرطوا في شكرها وزادوا نسيانا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The segment opens with the quoted assertion that the evil eye is real, but this fragment gives no reporting authority for it.
rows.anchor: " العين حق ". وفيه أخرج أبو نعيم في الحلية

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jābir reports that the Prophet said the evil eye can send a man to the grave and a camel to the cooking pot.
rows.anchor: وفيه أخرج أبو نعيم في الحلية عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports applying the preceding verses to wilāya are instances of application (jary), not exegesis, so the author omits them.
rows.anchor: وهناك روايات تطبق الآيات السابقة على الولاية وهي من الجري دون التفسير ولذلك لم نوردها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes al-ṭāghiya as a verbal noun like ṭughyān or ṭughwā, meaning the Thamūd were destroyed because of their rebellion; the Sun passage supports this sense.
rows.anchor: وقيل الطاغية مصدر كالطغيان والطغوى والمعنى فأما ثمود فاهلكوا بسبب طغيانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the first interpretation because the following verses enumerate modes of destruction; Thamūd’s al-ṭāghiya should therefore denote how they were destroyed.
rows.anchor: وأول الوجهين أنسب لسياق الآيات التالية حيث سيقت لبيان كيفية إهلاكهم من الإهلاك بالريح أو الأخذ الرابي أو طغيان الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarṣar is a cold wind blowing with great force; ʿātiya derives from transgression and denotes exceeding obedience and proper bounds.
rows.anchor: الصرصر الريح الباردة الشديدة الهبوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasḫīr here means subjecting or unleashing the wind upon them.
rows.anchor: تسخيرها عليهم تسليطها عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥusūm is the plural of ḥāsim, like shuhūd from shāhid, and derives from repeated cauterization in consecutive rounds.
rows.anchor: والحسوم جمع حاسم كشهود جمع شاهد من الحسم بمعنى تكرار الكي مرات متتالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥusūm is an adjective for the seven nights and eight days, which came successively without interruption.
rows.anchor: وهي صفة لسبع أي سبع ليال وثمانية أيام متتالية متتابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣarʿā is the plural of ṣarīʿ; aʿjāz is the plural of ʿajuz, the end or base of a thing; khāwiya means hollow inside and cast down.
rows.anchor: وصرعى جمع صريع وأعجاز جمع عجز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means whether any person remained alive; the sentence signifies that destruction overtook every one of them.
rows.anchor: والجملة كناية عن استيعاب الهلاك لهم جميعا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative treats bāqiya as the verbal noun baqāʾ, intended to mean a remnant; the author regards “surviving person” as closer.
rows.anchor: وقيل الباقية مصدر بمعنى البقاء وقد أريد به البقية وما قدمناه من المعنى أقرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh is the Pharaoh of Moses; those before him are earlier peoples who denied the truth; the overturned ones are the towns and population of Lot’s people.
rows.anchor: وبمن قبله الأمم المتقدمة عليه زمانا من المكذبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḫāṭiʾa is a verbal noun meaning error; coming with error means missing the path of servitude.
rows.anchor: مصدر بمعنى الخطأ والمراد بالمجيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject of “they disobeyed” is Pharaoh, the peoples before him, and the overturned towns; “the messenger” means messengers collectively.
rows.anchor: والمؤتفكات، والمراد بالرسول جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rābiya means increased or rising, from rabā, yarbū, rabwatan; the punishment was severe.
rows.anchor: والرابية الزائدة من ربا يربو ربوة إذا زاد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One alternative explains the punishment as exceeding other punishments.
rows.anchor: وقيل العقوبة الزائدة على سائر العقوبات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another alternative says the punishment was extraordinary and outside the ordinary course.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخارقة للعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water’s transgression refers to Noah’s flood, and al-jāriya is the ship.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى طوفان نوح والجارية السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressed people are described as carried in Noah’s ship, although their ancestors were literally aboard, because all people belong to one kind and one group’s state can be attributed to the whole.
rows.anchor: والمحمول في الحقيقة أسلافهم لكون الجميع نوعا واحدا ينسب حال البعض منه إلى الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains why they were carried; the feminine pronoun refers to the act of carrying, considered as an event.
rows.anchor: تعليل لحملهم في السفينة فضمير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flood and rescue were made a reminder, instructive example, and admonition.
rows.anchor: لنجعلها لكم أمرا تتذكرون به وعبرة تعتبرون بها وموعظة تتعظون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord’s general creative guidance equips every kind of creature to move toward its fitting perfection, as expressed in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: الذي أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans share this existential development with material creatures but also develop legislatively through chosen actions that form qualities and states in this life.
rows.anchor: والإنسان يشارك سائر الأنواع المادية في أن له استكمالا تكوينيا وسلوكا وجوديا نحو كماله الوجودي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those acquired dispositions constitute the human being’s lasting, happy life and the goal of human existence.
rows.anchor: وهي غاية وجود الإنسان التي تعيش بها عيشة سعيدة مؤبدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This need for chosen moral development motivates religious law through messengers, revealed books, and guidance, completing the proof against people.
rows.anchor: وهذا هو السبب الداعي إلى تشريع السنة الدينية بإرسال الرسل وإنزال الكتب والهداية إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revealed guidance first shows the straight path and leaves humans to choose gratitude or rejection.
rows.anchor: هذه هداية بمعنى إراءة الطريق وإعلام الصراط المستقيم الذي لا يسع الإنسان إلا أن يسلكه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the path yields a good, happy life; turning away brings lasting misery, while the proof is established either way.
rows.anchor: فإن لزم الصراط وسلكه حي بحياة طيبة سعيدة وإن تركه وأعرض عنه هلك بشقاء دائم وتمت عليه الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A reminder” points to guidance that shows the way: a reminder completes God’s proof but may or may not produce a response.
rows.anchor: فإن التذكرة لا تستوجب التذكر ممن ذكر بها بل ربما أثرت وربما تخلفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The aware ear points to guidance that carries a person to the goal; awareness is an instance of being led by divine guidance.
rows.anchor: فإن الوعي المذكور من مصاديق الاهتداء بالهداية الربوبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Awareness is not attributed only to God because the passage invites people and promises reward for responding; reward follows awareness as a human act, though it is also attributable to God.
rows.anchor: وأما الوعي فإنه وإن كان منسوبا إليه كما أنه منسوب إلى الإنسان لكن السياق سياق الدعوة وبيان الأجر والمثوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also indicates that external events can affect human actions.
rows.anchor: ويظهر من الآية الكريمة أن للحوادث الخارجية تأثيرا في أعمال الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the reverse influence, human actions shaping external events, to the verse about a town’s faith and piety opening blessings from heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: أن لأعمال الإنسان تأثيرا في الحوادث الخارجية وقد تقدم بعض الكلام فيه

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the reminder is for Muḥammad’s community: though many ships sank and traces vanished, the remains of Noah’s vessel were visible to them on Mount al-Jūdī.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن جريج في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Noah’s story in his commentary on Sūrat Hūd already supports this report.
rows.anchor: وتقدم ما يؤيد ذلك في قصة نوح في تفسير سورة هود

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Makhūl reports that when this verse was revealed, the Prophet asked God to make it ʿAlī’s ear; Makhūl adds that ʿAlī never forgot what he heard from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن مكحول قال لما نزلت { وتعيها أذن واعية } قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: مكحول
rows.claim: Makhūl says that ʿAlī would say he never forgot anything he heard from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال مكحول فكان علي يقول ما سمعت عن رسول الله شيئا فنسيته

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Burayda reports that the Prophet told ʿAlī God ordered him to draw ʿAlī close, teach him, and enable him to retain knowledge; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: عن بردة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم لعلي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reports the Prophet saying that God ordered him to teach ʿAlī to understand; the verse was revealed and the Prophet called ʿAlī the ear that retains his knowledge.
rows.anchor: عن علي قال قال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Burhān cites related reports through Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh from Abū ʿAbd Allāh, al-Kulaynī from him, and Ibn Bābawayh from Jābir from Abū Jaʿfar; it also cites reports ending with ʿAlī through ʿUmar b. ʿAlī, Burayda, and Zur b. Ḥubaysh.
rows.anchor: في تفسير البرهان عن سعد بن عبد الله بإسناده عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghāyat al-Marām counts sixteen reports on this point from both schools, while al-Burhān says Muḥammad b. al-ʿAbbās recorded thirty from Sunnī and Shīʿī sources.
rows.anchor: وقد روى في غاية المرام من طرق الفريقين ستة عشر حديثا في ذلك وقال في البرهان إن محمد بن العباس روى فيه ثلاثين حديثا
